Subject: Light Up a Life 2026

Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the bookshop window again this year.

Hilary asked us recently whether we were doing the tree, as her mum’s name was on it last year. Yes, Hilary, we are, and we would be very glad to see you and your sister.

Memory tags will be in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. There will be envelopes on the counter if you would rather take a tag home to write. You can remember anyone you are missing, whether or not they were cared for by the hospice. The tree is for everyone who is grieving.

This November marks seven years since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag on the tree I could hardly write it. These days I write it at the shop counter, with the same pen. I still think of him as I do it, of course, but it is a comfort to see his name there among so many others.

The tree will go into the window on Saturday 28 November, and we will switch the lights on at 4pm. The children from Gildencroft Primary are coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen is making her mince pies again. If last year is anything to go by, I would not leave it too late for a pie.

All the names on the tags will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December, at 3pm in the day centre. You do not have to attend the service for your person’s name to be read.

And please know that you are welcome to come in and stand by the tree for a while. You do not need to buy anything, and you do not need to explain. Sometimes it is enough just to be near it.

Thank you to everyone who remembered someone with us last year. There were 412 tags on the tree, each one for somebody loved and missed. It meant a great deal to have you share those names with us, and we will be glad to welcome you again.

Jean
